title: ActTail: Global Activation Sparsity in Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2603.12272v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Activation sparsity is a promising approach for accelerating large language model (LLM) inference by reducing computation and memory movement. However, existing activation sparsity methods typically apply uniform sparsity across projections, ignoring the heterogeneous statistical properties of Transformer weights and thereby amplifying performance degradation. In this paper, we propose ActTail, a TopK magnitude-based activation sparsity method with global activation sparsity allocation grounded in Heavy-Tailed Self-Regularization (HT-SR) theory. Specifically, we capture this heterogeneity via the heavy-tail exponent computed from each projection's empirical spectral density (ESD), which is used as a quantitative indicator to assign projection-specific sparsity budgets. Importantly, we provide a theoretical analysis that establishes an explicit relationship between the activation sparsity ratio and the heavy-tail exponent under the HT

translated_title: ActTail：大语言模型中的全局激活稀疏化

tldr: 提出基于重尾自正则化理论的ActTail方法，利用各投影层经验谱密度的重尾指数为其分配全局激活稀疏度预算，在加速大语言模型推理的同时缓解性能损失。
en_tdlr: ActTail assigns projection-specific global activation sparsity budgets based on heavy-tail exponents derived from empirical spectral density under HT-SR theory, accelerating LLM inference while mitigating performance degradation.
